"**Criminal**" is a song by Dominican singer [Natti Natasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natti_Natasha "Natti Natasha") and Puerto Rican singer [Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna "Ozuna"), released by [Pina Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pina_Records "Pina Records") on 18 August 2017\. Written by the two singers, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze, it is a [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") genre. The accompanying music video was directed by Nuno Gómes at an abandoned women's prison in [Vega Alta, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Alta,_Puerto_Rico "Vega Alta, Puerto Rico"), and portrays Ozuna as a prison director falling in love with a prisoner played by Natasha. It received over 1 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") within five months of its release and was the most watched music video by a female singer in 2017\.

The track was well received by music critics who found it catchy and praised it for giving reggaeton dance floor appeal. It received a number of award nominations, winning Best Collaboration at the 2018 [Soberano Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soberano_Awards "Soberano Awards"). "Criminal" became a [crossover success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_music "Crossover music") and helped relaunch Natasha's music career, becoming her first top five single on the US [Hot Latin Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Latin_Songs "Hot Latin Songs") chart since 2012's "[Dutty Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutty_Love_\(song\) "Dutty Love (song)")" and first chart-topper in Spain where it spent three consecutive weeks at number one. It also topped the charts in El Salvador, Paraguay, Peru and Spain, and reached the top 10 in 10 other Latin American countries.

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

"Criminal" was written by Natasha, Ozuna, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) Pina, Natasha's manager, sent Ozuna the song after two previously failed collaboration attempts, and Ozuna called it a "home run".[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Pina recalled, "After several months of trying to bring up the song, there was always a situation that would have discouraged anybody but, unlike me, I never got up with a 'no' in my head and continued without anything or anyone stopping me."[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Natasha regards "Criminal" as her second chance at a career in music and her first solo release where she had sufficient record label support. Regarding the writing process, she said: "To me, it's such a special song because I had the opportunity to write my part of the lyrics and I just really loved it. When Ozuna agreed, I was extremely excited and for some reason, I knew people were going to love it as much as we did."[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

It is a [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") genre.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music video")\]

[![Ozuna approaching Natti Natasha in an electric chair for a kiss.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/90/Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png/250px-Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png)

Ozuna approaching Natasha in an [electric chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_chair "Electric chair") for a kiss in the music video.

The accompanying music video was directed by Venezuelan director Nuno Gómes. It was filmed at a deactivated women's prison in [Vega Alta, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Alta,_Puerto_Rico "Vega Alta, Puerto Rico") in April 2017 and inspired by the music video for [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga")'s "[Telephone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_\(song\) "Telephone (song)")".[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-Vida_Primo-7) A storm hit Vega Alta a day before the video shoot, resulting in trucks getting stuck in mud and the video wardrobe getting wet. Gómes called it the worst filming day of his career.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6) Filming took nearly 20 hours.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Fashion designer Nelson Tavárez chose bold ensembles for Natasha's wardrobe to portray her character as empowered and confident.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

Natasha plays a prisoner trying to attract the attention of Ozuna, the prison director.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Vida_Primo-7) The clip starts with Natasha being escorted to the prison where Ozuna awaits. They are shown in several locations inside the prison with Natasha performing sensual dances for Ozuna. The video reaches a climax with Natasha sitting in an [electric chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_chair "Electric chair") and Ozuna approaching her for a kiss. Both are struck by electricity, but are shown together amid police alarms in the final scene.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

The video led [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube")'s weekly chart for two consecutive weeks in November 2017, ending [Luis Fonsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Fonsi "Luis Fonsi")'s 35-week run at number one with "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")".[\[10\]](#cite_note-Critica-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It surpassed 1 billion views on YouTube within five months of its 18 August 2017 release and was the most watched music video by a female artist in 2017\.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) "Criminal" is one of the 100 most viewed videos and eight most viewed Spanish-language videos on YouTube,[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) having received over 2\.7 billion views as of November 2025\.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Forbes-16) It is also both Natasha and Ozuna's most watched music video on the platform.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Forbes-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) Natasha said YouTube provided her with "the opportunity to reach other parts of the world, when before we depended on a label for that. It's definitely an achievement not only for me, but for Latina women. Before we did not have that reach."[\[10\]](#cite_note-Critica-10) *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* included "Criminal" at number 11 in its list of Top 25 Sexiest Latin Music Videos.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) Tommy Calle of *[Hoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoy_\(American_newspaper\) "Hoy (American newspaper)")* wrote that Natasha's "sensuality and beauty" in the video "stands out to the eye".[\[19\]](#cite_note-Hoy_Criminal-19)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

"Criminal" was well received by music critics. [Leila Cobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leila_Cobo "Leila Cobo") of *Billboard* described the song as "sexy without being vulgar" and said its "immediate catchiness" made it "a YouTube sensation".[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) Marjua Esteves of the same website wrote that it is "not your everyday fast-pumping reggaeton record, but a criminally slow-grinding jam".[\[21\]](#cite_note-Billboard-21) Raquel Reichard of *[The Fader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fader "The Fader")* called the track a "knockout" and an "earworm".[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) Writing for *[Maxim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_\(magazine\) "Maxim (magazine)")*, Brandon Friederich found the song "contagious" and wrote, "Even if you're a non-Spanish speaker, just try resisting the urge to sing the 'muy criminal'-laden chorus".[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) [Los 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_40 "Los 40")'s Alberto Palao Murcia commented, "I timidly gave the track a play expecting a more Latin rhythm that does not even reach the dance floor, but, to my surprise, by the second chorus I was already singing 'Criminal, Cri-Criminal..."[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Similarly, Tommy Calle of *Hoy* called it "an urban anthem that has managed to turn on the dance floor",[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) and "a catchy song that lifts everyone's spirits".[\[19\]](#cite_note-Hoy_Criminal-19)

*Billboard* placed "Criminal" at number 17 in its list of Top 20 Best Latin Songs of 2017\.[\[21\]](#cite_note-Billboard-21) [Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")'s Mike Wass gave the song an honorable mention in his list of The Best Latin Pop Songs of 2017\.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

2017 single by Natti Natasha and Ozuna

"Criminal"

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/43/Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal.png/250px-Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal.png)

[Single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_\(music\) "Single (music)") by [Natti Natasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natti_Natasha "Natti Natasha") and [Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna "Ozuna")

Language | Spanish

Released | 18 August 2017 (2017-08-18)

[Genre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre "Music genre") | [Reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton")

Length | 3:52

[Label](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_label "Record label") | [Pina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pina_Records "Pina Records")

[Songwriters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriter "Songwriter") | - [Natalia Gutiérrez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natti_Natasha "Natti Natasha") - [Juan Carlos Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna "Ozuna") - Egbert Rosa - Jesús Nieves - Rafael Pina - Vicente Saavedra

[Producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_producer "Record producer") | Haze

[Natti Natasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natti_Natasha "Natti Natasha") singles chronology

"[Otra Cosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otra_Cosa_\(song\) "Otra Cosa (song)")" (2016) "**Criminal**" (2017) "[Amantes de una Noche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amantes_de_una_Noche "Amantes de una Noche")" (2018)

[Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna "Ozuna") singles chronology

"[Se Preparó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Se_Preparó "Se Preparó")" (2017) "**Criminal**" (2017) "Egoísta" (2017)

Music video

["Criminal"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VqEbCxg2bNI) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_\(identifier\) "YouTube video (identifier)")

"**Criminal**" is a song by Dominican singer [Natti Natasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natti_Natasha "Natti Natasha") and Puerto Rican singer [Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna "Ozuna"), released by [Pina Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pina_Records "Pina Records") on 18 August 2017\. Written by the two singers, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze, it is a [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") genre. The accompanying music video was directed by Nuno Gómes at an abandoned women's prison in [Vega Alta, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Alta,_Puerto_Rico "Vega Alta, Puerto Rico"), and portrays Ozuna as a prison director falling in love with a prisoner played by Natasha. It received over 1 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") within five months of its release and was the most watched music video by a female singer in 2017\.

The track was well received by music critics who found it catchy and praised it for giving reggaeton dance floor appeal. It received a number of award nominations, winning Best Collaboration at the 2018 [Soberano Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soberano_Awards "Soberano Awards"). "Criminal" became a [crossover success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_music "Crossover music") and helped relaunch Natasha's music career, becoming her first top five single on the US [Hot Latin Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Latin_Songs "Hot Latin Songs") chart since 2012's "[Dutty Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutty_Love_\(song\) "Dutty Love (song)")" and first chart-topper in Spain where it spent three consecutive weeks at number one. It also topped the charts in El Salvador, Paraguay, Peru and Spain, and reached the top 10 in 10 other Latin American countries.

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

"Criminal" was written by Natasha, Ozuna, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) Pina, Natasha's manager, sent Ozuna the song after two previously failed collaboration attempts, and Ozuna called it a "home run".[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Pina recalled, "After several months of trying to bring up the song, there was always a situation that would have discouraged anybody but, unlike me, I never got up with a 'no' in my head and continued without anything or anyone stopping me."[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Natasha regards "Criminal" as her second chance at a career in music and her first solo release where she had sufficient record label support. Regarding the writing process, she said: "To me, it's such a special song because I had the opportunity to write my part of the lyrics and I just really loved it. When Ozuna agreed, I was extremely excited and for some reason, I knew people were going to love it as much as we did."[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

It is a [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") genre.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music video")\]

[![Ozuna approaching Natti Natasha in an electric chair for a kiss.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/90/Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png/250px-Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png)

Ozuna approaching Natasha in an [electric chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_chair "Electric chair") for a kiss in the music video.

The accompanying music video was directed by Venezuelan director Nuno Gómes. It was filmed at a deactivated women's prison in [Vega Alta, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Alta,_Puerto_Rico "Vega Alta, Puerto Rico") in April 2017 and inspired by the music video for [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga")'s "[Telephone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_\(song\) "Telephone (song)")".[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-Vida_Primo-7) A storm hit Vega Alta a day before the video shoot, resulting in trucks getting stuck in mud and the video wardrobe getting wet. Gómes called it the worst filming day of his career.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6) Filming took nearly 20 hours.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Fashion designer Nelson Tavárez chose bold ensembles for Natasha's wardrobe to portray her character as empowered and confident.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

Natasha plays a prisoner trying to attract the attention of Ozuna, the prison director.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Vida_Primo-7) The clip starts with Natasha being escorted to the prison where Ozuna awaits. They are shown in several locations inside the prison with Natasha performing sensual dances for Ozuna. The video reaches a climax with Natasha sitting in an [electric chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_chair "Electric chair") and Ozuna approaching her for a kiss. Both are struck by electricity, but are shown together amid police alarms in the final scene.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

The video led [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube")'s weekly chart for two consecutive weeks in November 2017, ending [Luis Fonsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Fonsi "Luis Fonsi")'s 35-week run at number one with "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")".[\[10\]](#cite_note-Critica-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It surpassed 1 billion views on YouTube within five months of its 18 August 2017 release and was the most watched music video by a female artist in 2017\.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) "Criminal" is one of the 100 most viewed videos and eight most viewed Spanish-language videos on YouTube,[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) having received over 2\.7 billion views as of November 2025\.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Forbes-16) It is also both Natasha and Ozuna's most watched music video on the platform.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Forbes-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) Natasha said YouTube provided her with "the opportunity to reach other parts of the world, when before we depended on a label for that. It's definitely an achievement not only for me, but for Latina women. Before we did not have that reach."[\[10\]](#cite_note-Critica-10) *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* included "Criminal" at number 11 in its list of Top 25 Sexiest Latin Music Videos.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) Tommy Calle of *[Hoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoy_\(American_newspaper\) "Hoy (American newspaper)")* wrote that Natasha's "sensuality and beauty" in the video "stands out to the eye".[\[19\]](#cite_note-Hoy_Criminal-19)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

"Criminal" was well received by music critics. [Leila Cobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leila_Cobo "Leila Cobo") of *Billboard* described the song as "sexy without being vulgar" and said its "immediate catchiness" made it "a YouTube sensation".[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) Marjua Esteves of the same website wrote that it is "not your everyday fast-pumping reggaeton record, but a criminally slow-grinding jam".[\[21\]](#cite_note-Billboard-21) Raquel Reichard of *[The Fader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fader "The Fader")* called the track a "knockout" and an "earworm".[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) Writing for *[Maxim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_\(magazine\) "Maxim (magazine)")*, Brandon Friederich found the song "contagious" and wrote, "Even if you're a non-Spanish speaker, just try resisting the urge to sing the 'muy criminal'-laden chorus".[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) [Los 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_40 "Los 40")'s Alberto Palao Murcia commented, "I timidly gave the track a play expecting a more Latin rhythm that does not even reach the dance floor, but, to my surprise, by the second chorus I was already singing 'Criminal, Cri-Criminal..."[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Similarly, Tommy Calle of *Hoy* called it "an urban anthem that has managed to turn on the dance floor",[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) and "a catchy song that lifts everyone's spirits".[\[19\]](#cite_note-Hoy_Criminal-19)

*Billboard* placed "Criminal" at number 17 in its list of Top 20 Best Latin Songs of 2017\.[\[21\]](#cite_note-Billboard-21) [Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")'s Mike Wass gave the song an honorable mention in his list of The Best Latin Pop Songs of 2017\.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

Natasha and Ozuna performed "Criminal" together at Calibash LA 2018 on 20 January and at the [Soberano Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soberano_Awards "Soberano Awards") on 21 March 2018\.[\[26\]](#cite_note-Soberano-26)[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) On 21 June 2018, Natasha performed the song at [VidCon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VidCon "VidCon") in [Anaheim, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim,_California "Anaheim, California").[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) She also performed the track at [KLVE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KLVE "KLVE")'s Las Qué Mandan event at the [Inglewood Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood_Forum "Inglewood Forum") on 17 November 2018\.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

"**Taki Taki**" is a song by French-Algerian DJ and record producer [DJ Snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Snake "DJ Snake"), featuring American singer [Selena Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selena_Gomez "Selena Gomez"), Puerto Rican singer [Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna "Ozuna"), and Dominican-American rapper [Cardi B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardi_B "Cardi B"). The song was released on 28 September 2018 as the second single from DJ Snake's second studio album *[Carte Blanche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carte_Blanche_\(DJ_Snake_album\) "Carte Blanche (DJ Snake album)")* (2019).[\[3\]](#cite_note-release-3) It was written and arranged by Bava (aka Ava Brignol), Belcalis Almanzar, Jorden Thorpe, Juan Carlos Ozuna Rosado, Juan G. Rivera, Max Borghetti, Selena Gomez, Vicente Saavedra, William Grigahcine. Ozuna opens the [moombahton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moombahton "Moombahton") and [reggaetón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song in Spanish, while Cardi B and Gomez follow in both English and Spanish.

The song's music video, directed by [Colin Tilley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Tilley "Colin Tilley"), was released on 9 October 2018 and features the four artists and several dancers inside of an ancient temple ruin within a volcano. The single reached number one in sixteen countries (including Argentina, Portugal and Spain), several of which were outside the [Hispanophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanophone "Hispanophone") market. It received a Diamond [certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification") in France, went [quadruple Platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") in the US, and won nine [music awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_award "Music award"). "Taki Taki" made Cardi B the first female rapper to top the [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") [Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-streamed_songs_on_Spotify#Weekly_number-one_songs "List of most-streamed songs on Spotify") chart,[\[4\]](#cite_note-spotify-4) extended her record as the first female rapper with [multiple billion-streamers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-streamed_songs_on_Spotify "List of most-streamed songs on Spotify") on the platform,[\[5\]](#cite_note-first-5) and made Ozuna the artist with the most one billion-view videos on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[\[6\]](#cite_note-billion-6)

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

In July 2018, Cardi B confirmed a collaboration with DJ Snake, Ozuna and [a third mystery guest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selena_Gomez "Selena Gomez").[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) The following month, [Selena Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selena_Gomez "Selena Gomez") and Cardi B teased a behind-the-scenes look at the song's music video shoot, which was filmed in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles").[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) On 17 September 2018, DJ Snake announced the release date.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition")\]

"Taki Taki", a reference to percussion and drum beats, is classed primarily as a moombahton and reggaetón song.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-rolling_stone-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) The whistle sample (in the [hook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hook_\(music\) "Hook (music)")) is from *Sounds of [KSHMR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KSHMR "KSHMR") Vol.2*. The track runs for three minutes and thirty-two seconds. Ozuna opens the track and provides the chorus, while Cardi B and Gomez follow, performing in English and Spanish.[\[12\]](#cite_note-rolling_stone-12)[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

Lyrically, the song sees Ozuna expressing his style of seduction, inviting his love interest to dance and interpreting what the other is thinking.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

Sheet music for "Taki Taki" showed the key of [C♯ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-sharp_minor "C-sharp minor") in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signature "Time signature") with a fast tempo of 96 beats per minute.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

## Music videos

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Music videos")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/2/2c/DJ_Snake_-_Taki_Taki_%28music_video_screenshot%29.png/250px-DJ_Snake_-_Taki_Taki_%28music_video_screenshot%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DJ_Snake_-_Taki_Taki_\(music_video_screenshot\).png)

From left to right, DJ Snake, Selena Gomez, Cardi B and Ozuna performing on an active [lava field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lava_field "Lava field").

The music video for "Taki Taki" premiered on 9 October 2018 on DJ Snake's YouTube channel. The video was directed by [Colin Tilley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Tilley "Colin Tilley"). A short teaser clip was shown at the [2018 American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2018 "American Music Awards of 2018").[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) The video is set in a [post-apocalyptic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-apocalyptic "Post-apocalyptic") world.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) The clip transitions with various landscapes showing the quartet together with a volcano in the background and in the solo scenes. These scenes include DJ Snake out in the storm near a [Range Rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_Rover "Range Rover"), Ozuna in a women-filled pit, Cardi B wearing a black bodysuit covered by a black cape accompanied by dancers, and Gomez in a green monochromatic outfit in the forest.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) It became the fifth fastest video of 2018 to reach 100 million views, and ranked among the top 10 fastest overall.[\[21\]](#cite_note-youtube-21) "Taki Taki" made Ozuna the artist with the most 1 billion-view videos on YouTube, with over seven videos.[\[6\]](#cite_note-billion-6) As of September 2025, the video has received over 2\.7 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[\[22\]](#cite_note-22)

A pixel video for "Taki Taki" was released on 11 December 2018 on YouTube, which featured animated pixel versions of the four artists dancing in various backgrounds.[\[23\]](#cite_note-pixel-23) The lyrics "Booty explota como *nagasaki*" (Booty blows up like Nagasaki) was criticized by Japanese media for belittling the [atomic bombing of Nagasaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_bombing_of_Nagasaki "Atomic bombing of Nagasaki") and the experience of its survivors.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) The lyrics were changed to "Booty explota como saki saki" (Booty blows up like saki saki), as requested by [Universal Music LLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_LLC "Universal Music LLC").[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taki_Taki#endnote_pixel)[\[26\]](#cite_note-26) This change in the lyrics was made in the official video. In France, the music video were criticized following suggestive scenes, Cardi B's sexual poses and was broadcast with blurring and a warning "Not advised to kids under 10 years old" or without warning.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

In the United States, "Taki Taki" debuted at number one on the [Hot Latin Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Latin_Songs "Hot Latin Songs"), where Ozuna replaced himself at the top with "[Te Boté](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Boté "Te Boté")", while bowing at number 27 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) It eventually reached number 11 on the Hot 100 during its fourth week.[\[28\]](#cite_note-Hot_100_peak-28) It became Gomez's 16th consecutive top 40 entry on the Hot 100, the longest active run of any artist.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) In the US [Latin Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Airplay "Latin Airplay") chart, it became the first number one for both DJ Snake and Gomez, the eighth for Ozuna and third for Cardi B.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

In addition, "Taki Taki" reached number one in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Greece, Guatemala, Honduras, Israel, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Portugal, Spain and Venezuela; the song also reached the top 10 in Belgium, Canada, Chile, Costa Rica, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Paraguay, the Philippines, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Sweden and Switzerland; as well as the top 20 in Austria, Finland, Ireland, Lebanon, New Zealand, Norway, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The song had a strong international impact, reaching the top of the [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") Global 50 chart where it has stayed for over four weeks. This made Cardi B the first female rapper to achieve such a feat.[\[4\]](#cite_note-spotify-4) It became DJ Snake's third song to reach [a billion streams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-streamed_songs_on_Spotify "List of most-streamed songs on Spotify") on Spotify, as well as Cardi's third and Gomez's and Ozuna's first.[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) Cardi B extended her record as the first female rapper with multiple billion-streamers, until being surpassed by black females rappers [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj") (7 songs) and [Doja Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doja_Cat "Doja Cat") (8 songs).[\[5\]](#cite_note-first-5) As of November 2018, the song has reached number one on the official charts of 15 countries and the top 10 of 33 countries around the world.

In France, the song debuted at number thirteen on September 26, 2018, becoming for three of four artists the highest-debut since Gomez's own solo song "[Good For You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_For_You_\(Selena_Gomez_song\) "Good For You (Selena Gomez song)")", served as the lead single from her second album [Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_\(Selena_Gomez_album\) "Revival (Selena Gomez album)"), which debuted at number 14\. Several weeks later and after [Christmas time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_music "Christmas music"), the song peaked at number 2 on January 5, 2019, blocked by "Tout Oublier" by [Belgian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") artist [Angèle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angèle "Angèle") becoming DJ Snake's sixth top ten, Gomez's third, Cardi B's second and last top ten and Ozuna's first top ten.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

Although it failed to peak atop, the single is currently certified diamond in France and spent 57 weeks, becoming Ozuna, Gomez's and Cardi B longest-running song and DJ Snake second longest running song after "[Loco Contigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loco_Contigo "Loco Contigo")".

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

Ozuna and Cardi B performed the song together live for the first time at the Dominican Republic's *Electric Paradise Festival* on 22 December 2018\.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) Ozuna also performed the song at the [2019 Premios Lo Nuestro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Lo_Nuestro_2019 "Premio Lo Nuestro 2019").[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) On 15 March 2019, he performed the song as part of a medley with "[Baila Baila Baila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baila_Baila_Baila "Baila Baila Baila")" on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")*. The only time in which all four artists—DJ Snake, Ozuna, Cardi B and Selena Gomez—took to the stage together was during DJ Snake's set at the 2019 [Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley_Music_and_Arts_Festival "Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival") in [Indio, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indio,_California "Indio, California"), much to the audience’s excitement. Ozuna featured the song during his headlining set and livestreamed performance at the [Viña Del Mar International Song Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viña_del_Mar_International_Song_Festival "Viña del Mar International Song Festival"), in [Valparaíso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valparaíso "Valparaíso"), [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile"), on 28 February 2020\.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) He also performed the song during the *[Celebrating America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrating_America "Celebrating America")* inauguration special in 2021\.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

["Taki Taki"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ixkoVwKQaJg) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_\(identifier\) "YouTube video (identifier)")

"**Taki Taki**" is a song by French-Algerian DJ and record producer [DJ Snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Snake "DJ Snake"), featuring American singer [Selena Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selena_Gomez "Selena Gomez"), Puerto Rican singer [Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna "Ozuna"), and Dominican-American rapper [Cardi B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardi_B "Cardi B"). The song was released on 28 September 2018 as the second single from DJ Snake's second studio album *[Carte Blanche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carte_Blanche_\(DJ_Snake_album\) "Carte Blanche (DJ Snake album)")* (2019).[\[3\]](#cite_note-release-3) It was written and arranged by Bava (aka Ava Brignol), Belcalis Almanzar, Jorden Thorpe, Juan Carlos Ozuna Rosado, Juan G. Rivera, Max Borghetti, Selena Gomez, Vicente Saavedra, William Grigahcine. Ozuna opens the [moombahton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moombahton "Moombahton") and [reggaetón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song in Spanish, while Cardi B and Gomez follow in both English and Spanish.

The song's music video, directed by [Colin Tilley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Tilley "Colin Tilley"), was released on 9 October 2018 and features the four artists and several dancers inside of an ancient temple ruin within a volcano. The single reached number one in sixteen countries (including Argentina, Portugal and Spain), several of which were outside the [Hispanophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanophone "Hispanophone") market. It received a Diamond [certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification") in France, went [quadruple Platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") in the US, and won nine [music awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_award "Music award"). "Taki Taki" made Cardi B the first female rapper to top the [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") [Global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-streamed_songs_on_Spotify#Weekly_number-one_songs "List of most-streamed songs on Spotify") chart,[\[4\]](#cite_note-spotify-4) extended her record as the first female rapper with [multiple billion-streamers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-streamed_songs_on_Spotify "List of most-streamed songs on Spotify") on the platform,[\[5\]](#cite_note-first-5) and made Ozuna the artist with the most one billion-view videos on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[\[6\]](#cite_note-billion-6)

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

In July 2018, Cardi B confirmed a collaboration with DJ Snake, Ozuna and [a third mystery guest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selena_Gomez "Selena Gomez").[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) The following month, [Selena Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selena_Gomez "Selena Gomez") and Cardi B teased a behind-the-scenes look at the song's music video shoot, which was filmed in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles").[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) On 17 September 2018, DJ Snake announced the release date.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition")\]

"Taki Taki", a reference to percussion and drum beats, is classed primarily as a moombahton and reggaetón song.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-rolling_stone-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) The whistle sample (in the [hook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hook_\(music\) "Hook (music)")) is from *Sounds of [KSHMR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KSHMR "KSHMR") Vol.2*. The track runs for three minutes and thirty-two seconds. Ozuna opens the track and provides the chorus, while Cardi B and Gomez follow, performing in English and Spanish.[\[12\]](#cite_note-rolling_stone-12)[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

Lyrically, the song sees Ozuna expressing his style of seduction, inviting his love interest to dance and interpreting what the other is thinking.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

Sheet music for "Taki Taki" showed the key of [C♯ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-sharp_minor "C-sharp minor") in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signature "Time signature") with a fast tempo of 96 beats per minute.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

## Music videos

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Music videos")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/2/2c/DJ_Snake_-_Taki_Taki_%28music_video_screenshot%29.png/250px-DJ_Snake_-_Taki_Taki_%28music_video_screenshot%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:DJ_Snake_-_Taki_Taki_\(music_video_screenshot\).png)

From left to right, DJ Snake, Selena Gomez, Cardi B and Ozuna performing on an active [lava field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lava_field "Lava field").

The music video for "Taki Taki" premiered on 9 October 2018 on DJ Snake's YouTube channel. The video was directed by [Colin Tilley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Tilley "Colin Tilley"). A short teaser clip was shown at the [2018 American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2018 "American Music Awards of 2018").[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) The video is set in a [post-apocalyptic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-apocalyptic "Post-apocalyptic") world.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) The clip transitions with various landscapes showing the quartet together with a volcano in the background and in the solo scenes. These scenes include DJ Snake out in the storm near a [Range Rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_Rover "Range Rover"), Ozuna in a women-filled pit, Cardi B wearing a black bodysuit covered by a black cape accompanied by dancers, and Gomez in a green monochromatic outfit in the forest.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) It became the fifth fastest video of 2018 to reach 100 million views, and ranked among the top 10 fastest overall.[\[21\]](#cite_note-youtube-21) "Taki Taki" made Ozuna the artist with the most 1 billion-view videos on YouTube, with over seven videos.[\[6\]](#cite_note-billion-6) As of September 2025, the video has received over 2\.7 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[\[22\]](#cite_note-22)

A pixel video for "Taki Taki" was released on 11 December 2018 on YouTube, which featured animated pixel versions of the four artists dancing in various backgrounds.[\[23\]](#cite_note-pixel-23) The lyrics "Booty explota como *nagasaki*" (Booty blows up like Nagasaki) was criticized by Japanese media for belittling the [atomic bombing of Nagasaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_bombing_of_Nagasaki "Atomic bombing of Nagasaki") and the experience of its survivors.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) The lyrics were changed to "Booty explota como saki saki" (Booty blows up like saki saki), as requested by [Universal Music LLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_LLC "Universal Music LLC").[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taki_Taki#endnote_pixel)[\[26\]](#cite_note-26) This change in the lyrics was made in the official video. In France, the music video were criticized following suggestive scenes, Cardi B's sexual poses and was broadcast with blurring and a warning "Not advised to kids under 10 years old" or without warning.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

In the United States, "Taki Taki" debuted at number one on the [Hot Latin Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Latin_Songs "Hot Latin Songs"), where Ozuna replaced himself at the top with "[Te Boté](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te_Boté "Te Boté")", while bowing at number 27 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) It eventually reached number 11 on the Hot 100 during its fourth week.[\[28\]](#cite_note-Hot_100_peak-28) It became Gomez's 16th consecutive top 40 entry on the Hot 100, the longest active run of any artist.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) In the US [Latin Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Airplay "Latin Airplay") chart, it became the first number one for both DJ Snake and Gomez, the eighth for Ozuna and third for Cardi B.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

In addition, "Taki Taki" reached number one in Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Greece, Guatemala, Honduras, Israel, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Portugal, Spain and Venezuela; the song also reached the top 10 in Belgium, Canada, Chile, Costa Rica, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Paraguay, the Philippines, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Sweden and Switzerland; as well as the top 20 in Austria, Finland, Ireland, Lebanon, New Zealand, Norway, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The song had a strong international impact, reaching the top of the [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") Global 50 chart where it has stayed for over four weeks. This made Cardi B the first female rapper to achieve such a feat.[\[4\]](#cite_note-spotify-4) It became DJ Snake's third song to reach [a billion streams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-streamed_songs_on_Spotify "List of most-streamed songs on Spotify") on Spotify, as well as Cardi's third and Gomez's and Ozuna's first.[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) Cardi B extended her record as the first female rapper with multiple billion-streamers, until being surpassed by black females rappers [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj") (7 songs) and [Doja Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doja_Cat "Doja Cat") (8 songs).[\[5\]](#cite_note-first-5) As of November 2018, the song has reached number one on the official charts of 15 countries and the top 10 of 33 countries around the world.

In France, the song debuted at number thirteen on September 26, 2018, becoming for three of four artists the highest-debut since Gomez's own solo song "[Good For You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_For_You_\(Selena_Gomez_song\) "Good For You (Selena Gomez song)")", served as the lead single from her second album [Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_\(Selena_Gomez_album\) "Revival (Selena Gomez album)"), which debuted at number 14\. Several weeks later and after [Christmas time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_music "Christmas music"), the song peaked at number 2 on January 5, 2019, blocked by "Tout Oublier" by [Belgian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") artist [Angèle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angèle "Angèle") becoming DJ Snake's sixth top ten, Gomez's third, Cardi B's second and last top ten and Ozuna's first top ten.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

Although it failed to peak atop, the single is currently certified diamond in France and spent 57 weeks, becoming Ozuna, Gomez's and Cardi B longest-running song and DJ Snake second longest running song after "[Loco Contigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loco_Contigo "Loco Contigo")".

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Taki_Taki&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

Ozuna and Cardi B performed the song together live for the first time at the Dominican Republic's *Electric Paradise Festival* on 22 December 2018\.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) Ozuna also performed the song at the [2019 Premios Lo Nuestro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Lo_Nuestro_2019 "Premio Lo Nuestro 2019").[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) On 15 March 2019, he performed the song as part of a medley with "[Baila Baila Baila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baila_Baila_Baila "Baila Baila Baila")" on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")*. The only time in which all four artists—DJ Snake, Ozuna, Cardi B and Selena Gomez—took to the stage together was during DJ Snake's set at the 2019 [Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley_Music_and_Arts_Festival "Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival") in [Indio, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indio,_California "Indio, California"), much to the audience’s excitement. Ozuna featured the song during his headlining set and livestreamed performance at the [Viña Del Mar International Song Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viña_del_Mar_International_Song_Festival "Viña del Mar International Song Festival"), in [Valparaíso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valparaíso "Valparaíso"), [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile"), on 28 February 2020\.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) He also performed the song during the *[Celebrating America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrating_America "Celebrating America")* inauguration special in 2021\.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

"Mayores" is a song by American singer Becky G and Puerto Rican rapper Bad Bunny. Written by Mario Caceres, Servando Primera, Saul Castillo, Bad Bunny, and Patrick Ingunza, it was released by Kemosabe, RCA Records and Sony Music Latin as the lead single from Gomez's debut studio album Mala Santa on July 14, 2017.[2][3]

"Mayores" topped the charts in Spain, Ecuador, Chile, Paraguay, Peru, Bolivia, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama and El Salvador, while peaking at number 3 on the Billboard Hot Latin Songs chart.[4] The music video for the song was released on YouTube on July 13, 2017, and has accumulated over 2.5 billion views on YouTube as of October 2025.[5]

Background[edit]
Gomez explained that the song originated as a "joke" after having confirmed her relationship with soccer player Sebastian Lletget, who is five years older than her. She started using the hashtag "#6DaysTillMAYORES" on Twitter which eventually started trending. A number became lower with each passing day, until it reached "#MAYORESOutNow".

Chart performance[edit]
"Mayores" debuted at number 12 on the Hot Latin Songs chart, making it Gomez's highest debut peak position on that chart. The song eventually peaked at number 3 on the charts.

The song also debuted at number 72 on the Spanish PROMUSICAE chart. It rose to number 4 four weeks later, making it her highest-peaking position, surpassing the number 37 peak of "Shower". It later reached number one.

The song eventually charted on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number 74. This marked Gomez’s fourth appearance on the chart in over two years, following her top-twenty hit “Shower” (2014), her collaboration with Cher Lloyd, “Oath” (2012), which peaked at number 73, and “Can't Stop Dancin'” (2014), which reached number 88 in early 2015. The song also earned Bad Bunny his first entry on the Hot 100.

Music video[edit]
The music video, filmed in Los Angeles and San Francisco, was uploaded on Gomez's Vevo account on July 13, 2017. As of October 2025, it has received over 2.5 billion views on YouTube.[6]

Premise[edit]
The clip sees Gomez lying on a couch spliced with scenes of her and Bad Bunny at a bar. Casper Smart, playing an older, wealthy man, enters the bar and is attracted to Gomez. He takes her to his house as Bad Bunny raps his verses at the bar. These scenes are also cut with the singers performing on the roof of the Hotel Rosslyn Annex at night. Gomez seduces Smart and handcuffs him to the bed. She plays with his watch before getting off the bed and leaving with a bag full of money. Bad Bunny appears to be waiting for her, and they kiss before getting in the car. The video ends with the duo driving off.

Live performances[edit]
Due to the song becoming a huge success, Gomez was invited to perform it at several radio stations and during interviews. She sang the song regular and acoustic at iHeart Radio Mi Música. She also sang it in Spain in La Vida Moderna and Sale el Sol in acoustic, and regular on Operación Triunfo. Her performance on the latter garnered some attention due to a change in the lyrics at the request of the producers due to them thinking they were "too sexual". Although Gomez agreed, she later stated it bothered her and said she accepted "out of respect" and because it was "a great opportunity", but believes that it wouldn't be done to a man, listing Ozuna and Enrique Iglesias as examples.[7]

Gomez performed the song with Bad Bunny at the Latin American Music Awards of 2017, which she also hosted; the performance was later uploaded to YouTube and has garnered over 91 million views.[8] The song was included on her setlist as an opening act for Fifth Harmony's 2017 PSA Tour and on her own tour in 2018. She sang the song last in her performance at Viña del Mar on March 2, 2019. Gomez and Bad Bunny performed the song at the latter's X 100pPre Tour on March 8 and April 22, 2019.[9] Gomez included "Mayores" in three medleys: the first at the 2019 Latin American Music Awards together with "Sin Pijama" and "Mala Santa", before receiving the Extraordinary Evolution Award from Pitbull. The second time was at the 2019 MTV Europe Music Awards, this time with "24/7", a track from her debut album replacing "Mala Santa".[10] The third time was at the LOS40 Music Awards 2019 with the original medley. All three performances had different arrangements. In the latter performance Gomez rewrote Bad Bunny's verse with lyrics from her "side of the relationship", including a reference to her feature in "Dura (Remix)" with Daddy Yankee, Natti Natasha, and the rapper.[11] Gomez performed the song at the Coachella 2023 on April 14 and 21, 2023.[12]

"Mayores" is a song by American singer Becky G and Puerto Rican rapper Bad Bunny. Written by Mario Caceres, Servando Primera, Saul Castillo, Bad Bunny, and Patrick Ingunza, it was released by Kemosabe, RCA Records and Sony Music Latin as the lead single from Gomez's debut studio album Mala Santa on July 14, 2017.[2][3]

"Mayores" topped the charts in Spain, Ecuador, Chile, Paraguay, Peru, Bolivia, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama and El Salvador, while peaking at number 3 on the Billboard Hot Latin Songs chart.[4] The music video for the song was released on YouTube on July 13, 2017, and has accumulated over 2.5 billion views on YouTube as of October 2025.[5]

Background[edit]
Gomez explained that the song originated as a "joke" after having confirmed her relationship with soccer player Sebastian Lletget, who is five years older than her. She started using the hashtag "#6DaysTillMAYORES" on Twitter which eventually started trending. A number became lower with each passing day, until it reached "#MAYORESOutNow".

Chart performance[edit]
"Mayores" debuted at number 12 on the Hot Latin Songs chart, making it Gomez's highest debut peak position on that chart. The song eventually peaked at number 3 on the charts.

The song also debuted at number 72 on the Spanish PROMUSICAE chart. It rose to number 4 four weeks later, making it her highest-peaking position, surpassing the number 37 peak of "Shower". It later reached number one.

The song eventually charted on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number 74. This marked Gomez’s fourth appearance on the chart in over two years, following her top-twenty hit “Shower” (2014), her collaboration with Cher Lloyd, “Oath” (2012), which peaked at number 73, and “Can't Stop Dancin'” (2014), which reached number 88 in early 2015. The song also earned Bad Bunny his first entry on the Hot 100.

Music video[edit]
The music video, filmed in Los Angeles and San Francisco, was uploaded on Gomez's Vevo account on July 13, 2017. As of October 2025, it has received over 2.5 billion views on YouTube.[6]

Premise[edit]
The clip sees Gomez lying on a couch spliced with scenes of her and Bad Bunny at a bar. Casper Smart, playing an older, wealthy man, enters the bar and is attracted to Gomez. He takes her to his house as Bad Bunny raps his verses at the bar. These scenes are also cut with the singers performing on the roof of the Hotel Rosslyn Annex at night. Gomez seduces Smart and handcuffs him to the bed. She plays with his watch before getting off the bed and leaving with a bag full of money. Bad Bunny appears to be waiting for her, and they kiss before getting in the car. The video ends with the duo driving off.

Live performances[edit]
Due to the song becoming a huge success, Gomez was invited to perform it at several radio stations and during interviews. She sang the song regular and acoustic at iHeart Radio Mi Música. She also sang it in Spain in La Vida Moderna and Sale el Sol in acoustic, and regular on Operación Triunfo. Her performance on the latter garnered some attention due to a change in the lyrics at the request of the producers due to them thinking they were "too sexual". Although Gomez agreed, she later stated it bothered her and said she accepted "out of respect" and because it was "a great opportunity", but believes that it wouldn't be done to a man, listing Ozuna and Enrique Iglesias as examples.[7]

Gomez performed the song with Bad Bunny at the Latin American Music Awards of 2017, which she also hosted; the performance was later uploaded to YouTube and has garnered over 91 million views.[8] The song was included on her setlist as an opening act for Fifth Harmony's 2017 PSA Tour and on her own tour in 2018. She sang the song last in her performance at Viña del Mar on March 2, 2019. Gomez and Bad Bunny performed the song at the latter's X 100pPre Tour on March 8 and April 22, 2019.[9] Gomez included "Mayores" in three medleys: the first at the 2019 Latin American Music Awards together with "Sin Pijama" and "Mala Santa", before receiving the Extraordinary Evolution Award from Pitbull. The second time was at the 2019 MTV Europe Music Awards, this time with "24/7", a track from her debut album replacing "Mala Santa".[10] The third time was at the LOS40 Music Awards 2019 with the original medley. All three performances had different arrangements. In the latter performance Gomez rewrote Bad Bunny's verse with lyrics from her "side of the relationship", including a reference to her feature in "Dura (Remix)" with Daddy Yankee, Natti Natasha, and the rapper.[11] Gomez performed the song at the Coachella 2023 on April 14 and 21, 2023.[12]

"Sin Pijama" is a song by American singer Becky G and Dominican singer Natti Natasha. It was written by the two singers, Nate Campany, Kyle Sherear, Rafael Pina, Mau y Ricky, Jon Leone, Camilo Echeverry and its producers Daddy Yankee and Gaby Music. The song and its music video were released by on April 20, 2018. It became both Gomez and Natasha's third top 10 hit on US Hot Latin Songs and has reached number one in Bolivia, Chile, El Salvador and Spain as well as the top 10 in Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Peru and Uruguay. "Sin Pijama" received a Latin platinum certification in the US and surpassed 100 million views on YouTube/Vevo within 3 weeks of its release. As of 2022, it has been certified 38-times Latin platinum.

Background[edit]
"Sin Pijama"  written by Becky G, Natti Natasha, Nate Campany, Kyle Sherear, Rafael Pina, Daddy Yankee, Gaby Music, Mau y Ricky, Jon Leone and Camilo Echeverry.[2] Gomez first wrote the song during a writing session with Mau y Ricky around two years prior to its release. According to her, she had to keep fighting and reminding her record label about "Sin Pijama", and it was not until she suggested a collaboration with Natasha that the track progressed.[3] In a discussion with Natasha for Vevo, Gomez recalled, "When I heard that you loved the song and that you wanted to do your thing on it, I was like, relieved, 'She gets it. Perfect!"[4] She described Yankee, Gaby Music and Natasha's consecutive involvement as the missing puzzle pieces coming together.[3] With "Sin Pijama", Gomez wanted to continue the female empowerment theme of her 2017 single "Mayores".[5] Regarding the song, Natasha said, "Women connect with the most sensual songs because they want to see themselves portrayed in music as they really feel."[6] Gomez confessed that the song originally intended to feature Karol G, Leslie Grace and Lali, adding: "There's more women in the Latin music space right now, and I'm proud to call them my friends."[7]

Music and lyrics[edit]
Composed in 44 time, "Sin Pijama" is a reggaeton song spanning three minutes and eight seconds.[2][8][9] It has an urban and Latin rhythm, and is described by Gomez as more reggaeton than "Mayores".[1][5][10] The lyrics discuss a desire for sex, using double entendres for a couple not being able to sleep because one of them left their pajamas at home.[11][12] It includes references to smoking cannabis.[13] The singer said the lyrics detail "the great fantasy of men" to know what happens between women at a sleepover.[5] She regards "Sin Pijama" as empowering for women owning their sexuality, a theme she believes is uncommon and should be accepted, specifically in Latin music.[4]

According to Telemundo, the lyrics caused controversy for its explicit themes to which Becky G responded to in an interview for Suelta la Sopa, saying: "I am a woman; I am 21 years old and I am not the father of your children. If you do not want your daughter or your son to listen to my music, it's your decision and I respect it totally. But if you're going to let your daughter or your son listen to Maluma, Bad Bunny or Ozuna because they're men, that's the problem. There are so many things that I can not understand. It makes me very sad."[13] Spanish singer Beatriz Luengo criticized the song's intended feminist message and claimed that it instead spoke of sexuality to only please men, citing it as "men writing what they would like women to say."[14]

Critical reception[edit]
"Sin Pijama" received positive reviews from music critics upon release. Suzette Fernandez of Billboard magazine said it proves "women are taking control in Latin music" and "can also dominate the urban genre."[15] She deemed the song "a girl power anthem".[1] In Hoy, Sergio Burstein regarded its "duo between two famous ladies at the rhythm of reggaeton" as a first for Latin music and wrote, instead of pushing feminism in culture, it uses sex in advertising to show that "girls just wanna have fun."[16] Similarly, Bárbara Figueroa González of Ronda magazine believed "Sin Pijama" marked "a great step for women in the urban genre."[17] La República called the track "catchy",[18] while Clarín viewed it as "a sensual hit, provocative and catchy".[19] EFE's David Villafranca wrote, "With a rhythm and a sexy air that directly resemble her with 'Mayores', 'Sin Pijama' allowed Becky G to expand her list of collaborations".[5] Mike Wass of Idolator found the song "sexy" and said Becky G "has gone from strength to strength".[10]

Chart performance[edit]
"Sin Pijama" became both Gomez and Natasha's third top 10 hit on the US Hot Latin Songs chart where it debuted at number 10, marking Natasha's highest debut on the chart. It received 5 million streams, 2 million audience impressions and sold 7,000 copies in its first week.[20] The song rose to number four in its fifteenth week,[21] and reached number 70 on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart. It was certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) within 18 days of its release.[22] Outside the U.S., "Sin Pijama" entered the Productores de Música de España (PROMUSICAE) singles chart at number 28.[23] It has since reached number one,[24] thus making it both Gomez and Natti Natasha's second song to top the chart in Spain.[25][26] PROMUSICAE certified the single Platinum for sales of 40,000 units in the region.[27] Across Latin America, the song has charted in the top ten of the Monitor Latino charts in El Salvador (number four),[28] Guatemala and Uruguay (number six),[29][30] Chile and Nicaragua (number three),[31][32] Honduras (number eight),[33] and Peru (number ten).[34]

Music video[edit]
Development[edit]
External images The first and second page of the music video synopsis Becky G sent to Duran in a mobile note.[35]
The music video for "Sin Pijama" was directed by Venezuelan director Daniel Duran in a one-day shoot in New York.[9] Gomez came up with the video concept nearly a year prior to sending it to Duran in a mobile note in January 2018 and revealed that "it took a lot of fight" for it to happen.[35] Although she had a different idea for the video's ending, Gomez said it was her favorite part because it represented reality and did not want sexuality to be the only thing she is associated with. The singer met Natasha for the first time on the music video set, but said they had "instant chemistry".[4][35] In her synopsis note, she aspired for the fashion to resemble that of Victoria's Secret.[35] The video includes a cameo appearance by American singer Prince Royce.[12] It premiered on Gomez's Vevo channel at 00:00 PST on April 20, 2018.[11]

Synopsis[edit]
Natasha and Becky G in a scene from Royce's dream in the music video.
The video begins with Royce and a friend at a recording studio where they talk about inviting Gomez and her friends to join them.[36] Royce contacts Gomez through FaceTime to no answer and then sees on Twitter that they are having a girls night and begins to imagine about what the night would be like.[35] The song and dream sequence then start with Gomez and Natasha entering a lavish mansion party in contrasting white and black dresses.[15][16] Performance pieces take place around the mansion as they wear several lingerie outfits, faux fur and jewelry.[19] The singers are seen drinking champagne, laying on a bed, playing pool, and partaking in a photo shoot and pillow fight.[37] In a plot twist, they are shown having a sleepover in pajamas with face masks on, eating popcorn before Gomez receives a FaceTime from Royce to her delight.[11] According to her, this scene is intended as comic relief and a reflection of what actually happens at girl sleepovers.[35]

Reception[edit]
The music video was well received by most critics. Writing for La Nación, Felipe Gerjado regarded it as "great sensuality",[36] while Maxim magazine found it "sultry".[37] La Opinión called the video "the most daring moment in Becky G's career."[38] Similarly, El Heraldo described the visual as "lace, lingerie and lots of skin", noting that the singers "show their most daring side."[39] Sergio Burstein of Hoy opined that it had "obvious lesbian connotations".[16] E! Online Latino said, "Becky G follows her personal instinct and triumphs."[35] Conversely, Alberto Murcia of Los 40 believed the dream concept should have been excluded, questioning if "the only way a woman has to live her sexuality is within a man's fantasy?"[11]

The video surpassed 100 million views on YouTube/Vevo on May 9, 2018 (less than 3 weeks after its premiere).[22] It was the most-watched YouTube video in Colombia for April 2018, according to National-Report,[40] and reached number two on the US YouTube Songs chart published by Billboard.[41] The music video reached one billion views in October 2018. It was the most-watched music video by a female artist in its year of release.[42] The clip surpassed "Side to Side" by Ariana Grande featuring Nicki Minaj as the most-viewed female collaboration and became the first to achieve 2 billion views.

Live performances[edit]
Becky G and Natti Natasha performed "Sin Pijama" together for the first time at the MTV Millennial Awards on June 3, 2018.[43] The duo performed the song again at the 2018 Premios Juventud on July 22, 2018.[44] The song has since been included inn Gomez's performances, usually being the second-to-last or last to be performed. Gomez and Natasha performed the song together at the Coachella 2023 on April 14 and 21, 2023.[45]

"Sin Pijama" is a song by American singer Becky G and Dominican singer Natti Natasha. It was written by the two singers, Nate Campany, Kyle Sherear, Rafael Pina, Mau y Ricky, Jon Leone, Camilo Echeverry and its producers Daddy Yankee and Gaby Music. The song and its music video were released by on April 20, 2018. It became both Gomez and Natasha's third top 10 hit on US Hot Latin Songs and has reached number one in Bolivia, Chile, El Salvador and Spain as well as the top 10 in Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Peru and Uruguay. "Sin Pijama" received a Latin platinum certification in the US and surpassed 100 million views on YouTube/Vevo within 3 weeks of its release. As of 2022, it has been certified 38-times Latin platinum.

Background[edit]
"Sin Pijama"  written by Becky G, Natti Natasha, Nate Campany, Kyle Sherear, Rafael Pina, Daddy Yankee, Gaby Music, Mau y Ricky, Jon Leone and Camilo Echeverry.[2] Gomez first wrote the song during a writing session with Mau y Ricky around two years prior to its release. According to her, she had to keep fighting and reminding her record label about "Sin Pijama", and it was not until she suggested a collaboration with Natasha that the track progressed.[3] In a discussion with Natasha for Vevo, Gomez recalled, "When I heard that you loved the song and that you wanted to do your thing on it, I was like, relieved, 'She gets it. Perfect!"[4] She described Yankee, Gaby Music and Natasha's consecutive involvement as the missing puzzle pieces coming together.[3] With "Sin Pijama", Gomez wanted to continue the female empowerment theme of her 2017 single "Mayores".[5] Regarding the song, Natasha said, "Women connect with the most sensual songs because they want to see themselves portrayed in music as they really feel."[6] Gomez confessed that the song originally intended to feature Karol G, Leslie Grace and Lali, adding: "There's more women in the Latin music space right now, and I'm proud to call them my friends."[7]

Music and lyrics[edit]
Composed in 44 time, "Sin Pijama" is a reggaeton song spanning three minutes and eight seconds.[2][8][9] It has an urban and Latin rhythm, and is described by Gomez as more reggaeton than "Mayores".[1][5][10] The lyrics discuss a desire for sex, using double entendres for a couple not being able to sleep because one of them left their pajamas at home.[11][12] It includes references to smoking cannabis.[13] The singer said the lyrics detail "the great fantasy of men" to know what happens between women at a sleepover.[5] She regards "Sin Pijama" as empowering for women owning their sexuality, a theme she believes is uncommon and should be accepted, specifically in Latin music.[4]

According to Telemundo, the lyrics caused controversy for its explicit themes to which Becky G responded to in an interview for Suelta la Sopa, saying: "I am a woman; I am 21 years old and I am not the father of your children. If you do not want your daughter or your son to listen to my music, it's your decision and I respect it totally. But if you're going to let your daughter or your son listen to Maluma, Bad Bunny or Ozuna because they're men, that's the problem. There are so many things that I can not understand. It makes me very sad."[13] Spanish singer Beatriz Luengo criticized the song's intended feminist message and claimed that it instead spoke of sexuality to only please men, citing it as "men writing what they would like women to say."[14]

Critical reception[edit]
"Sin Pijama" received positive reviews from music critics upon release. Suzette Fernandez of Billboard magazine said it proves "women are taking control in Latin music" and "can also dominate the urban genre."[15] She deemed the song "a girl power anthem".[1] In Hoy, Sergio Burstein regarded its "duo between two famous ladies at the rhythm of reggaeton" as a first for Latin music and wrote, instead of pushing feminism in culture, it uses sex in advertising to show that "girls just wanna have fun."[16] Similarly, Bárbara Figueroa González of Ronda magazine believed "Sin Pijama" marked "a great step for women in the urban genre."[17] La República called the track "catchy",[18] while Clarín viewed it as "a sensual hit, provocative and catchy".[19] EFE's David Villafranca wrote, "With a rhythm and a sexy air that directly resemble her with 'Mayores', 'Sin Pijama' allowed Becky G to expand her list of collaborations".[5] Mike Wass of Idolator found the song "sexy" and said Becky G "has gone from strength to strength".[10]

Chart performance[edit]
"Sin Pijama" became both Gomez and Natasha's third top 10 hit on the US Hot Latin Songs chart where it debuted at number 10, marking Natasha's highest debut on the chart. It received 5 million streams, 2 million audience impressions and sold 7,000 copies in its first week.[20] The song rose to number four in its fifteenth week,[21] and reached number 70 on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart. It was certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) within 18 days of its release.[22] Outside the U.S., "Sin Pijama" entered the Productores de Música de España (PROMUSICAE) singles chart at number 28.[23] It has since reached number one,[24] thus making it both Gomez and Natti Natasha's second song to top the chart in Spain.[25][26] PROMUSICAE certified the single Platinum for sales of 40,000 units in the region.[27] Across Latin America, the song has charted in the top ten of the Monitor Latino charts in El Salvador (number four),[28] Guatemala and Uruguay (number six),[29][30] Chile and Nicaragua (number three),[31][32] Honduras (number eight),[33] and Peru (number ten).[34]

Music video[edit]
Development[edit]
External images The first and second page of the music video synopsis Becky G sent to Duran in a mobile note.[35]
The music video for "Sin Pijama" was directed by Venezuelan director Daniel Duran in a one-day shoot in New York.[9] Gomez came up with the video concept nearly a year prior to sending it to Duran in a mobile note in January 2018 and revealed that "it took a lot of fight" for it to happen.[35] Although she had a different idea for the video's ending, Gomez said it was her favorite part because it represented reality and did not want sexuality to be the only thing she is associated with. The singer met Natasha for the first time on the music video set, but said they had "instant chemistry".[4][35] In her synopsis note, she aspired for the fashion to resemble that of Victoria's Secret.[35] The video includes a cameo appearance by American singer Prince Royce.[12] It premiered on Gomez's Vevo channel at 00:00 PST on April 20, 2018.[11]

Synopsis[edit]
Natasha and Becky G in a scene from Royce's dream in the music video.
The video begins with Royce and a friend at a recording studio where they talk about inviting Gomez and her friends to join them.[36] Royce contacts Gomez through FaceTime to no answer and then sees on Twitter that they are having a girls night and begins to imagine about what the night would be like.[35] The song and dream sequence then start with Gomez and Natasha entering a lavish mansion party in contrasting white and black dresses.[15][16] Performance pieces take place around the mansion as they wear several lingerie outfits, faux fur and jewelry.[19] The singers are seen drinking champagne, laying on a bed, playing pool, and partaking in a photo shoot and pillow fight.[37] In a plot twist, they are shown having a sleepover in pajamas with face masks on, eating popcorn before Gomez receives a FaceTime from Royce to her delight.[11] According to her, this scene is intended as comic relief and a reflection of what actually happens at girl sleepovers.[35]

Reception[edit]
The music video was well received by most critics. Writing for La Nación, Felipe Gerjado regarded it as "great sensuality",[36] while Maxim magazine found it "sultry".[37] La Opinión called the video "the most daring moment in Becky G's career."[38] Similarly, El Heraldo described the visual as "lace, lingerie and lots of skin", noting that the singers "show their most daring side."[39] Sergio Burstein of Hoy opined that it had "obvious lesbian connotations".[16] E! Online Latino said, "Becky G follows her personal instinct and triumphs."[35] Conversely, Alberto Murcia of Los 40 believed the dream concept should have been excluded, questioning if "the only way a woman has to live her sexuality is within a man's fantasy?"[11]

The video surpassed 100 million views on YouTube/Vevo on May 9, 2018 (less than 3 weeks after its premiere).[22] It was the most-watched YouTube video in Colombia for April 2018, according to National-Report,[40] and reached number two on the US YouTube Songs chart published by Billboard.[41] The music video reached one billion views in October 2018. It was the most-watched music video by a female artist in its year of release.[42] The clip surpassed "Side to Side" by Ariana Grande featuring Nicki Minaj as the most-viewed female collaboration and became the first to achieve 2 billion views.

Live performances[edit]
Becky G and Natti Natasha performed "Sin Pijama" together for the first time at the MTV Millennial Awards on June 3, 2018.[43] The duo performed the song again at the 2018 Premios Juventud on July 22, 2018.[44] The song has since been included inn Gomez's performances, usually being the second-to-last or last to be performed. Gomez and Natasha performed the song together at the Coachella 2023 on April 14 and 21, 2023.[45]

        f = p.split('#')
        # w#h#totalthumbs#cols#rows#interval#name#sig
        w,h,total,cols,rows,interval,names,sig = f[0],f[1],f[2],f[3],f[4],f[5],f[6],f[7]
        levels[interval] = (int(w),int(h),int(cols),int(rows),int(total),names,sig)

                t = im.crop((c*w, r*h, (c+1)*w, (r+1)*h))

                thumbs.append(t.getpixel((0,0)))
        time.sleep(0.3)
    results[k] = {'name':name,'vid':vid,'dur':dur,'interval':interval,'n':len(thumbs),'thumbs':thumbs}
    print(k, name, 'dur', dur, 'thumbs', len(thumbs), 'interval~', interval)

import json

sb = json.load(open('storyboards.json'))

    for y in range(h):
        p = px[x,y]; r+=p[0]; g+=p[1]; b+=p[2]
    cols.append((r/h, g/h, b/h))

def interp(thumbs, n):
    m = len(thumbs)
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        t = (i+0.5)/n*m - 0.5
        t = max(0, min(m-1, t))
        i0 = int(t); i1 = min(m-1, i0+1); f = t-i0
        a,b_ = thumbs[i0], thumbs[i1]
        out.append(tuple(a[c]*(1-f)+b_[c]*f for c in range(3)))
    return out

# scale factor: normalize by mean abs deviation of barcode colors
import statistics
flat = [c for col in cols for c in col]
mu = sum(flat)/len(flat)
scale = (sum(abs(c-mu) for c in flat)/len(flat)) or 1

print(f"{'cand':4s} {'name':38s} {'dur':>4s} {'n':>4s} {'MSE':>8s} {'normErr':>8s} {'corr':>6s}")

    for x in range(w):

        for c in range(3):

            se += d*d
            num += (c0[c]-mu)*(c1[c]-mu)

    mse = se/(w*3)
    corr = num/((den**0.5)*(se and (se - num**2/ (den if den else 1)) and 1 or 1) or 1)  # messy; compute properly below
    # proper pearson
    ys = [c1 for s in seq for c1 in s]

    sxy = sum((a-mx)*(b-my) for a,b in zip(xs,ys))
